newsitem.title: USA: Clinton has big lead, Congress fight close - poll.
newsitem.headline: Clinton has big lead, Congress fight close - poll.

text.p: One week before election day President Clinton held a commanding lead over Republican challenger Bob Dole but the battle for control of Congress is getting closer, according to a Los Angeles Times poll released Tuesday.
The newspaper reported that while Clinton has bolstered his standing among voters since early October, the Republican party is picking up support in congressional races.

The poll found that close to 90 percent of likely voters have firmly settled on their choice for president, and that Clinton leads Dole by 51 percent to 34 percent, with Reform Party candidate Ross Perot trailing at 12 percent.
Clinton's 17 percentage point lead over Dole compares with a 12 percentage point lead in a Times poll taken at the beginning of October.

But the Democratic Party lead in the battle for Congress has slipped to just four percentage points, with a growing number of voters saying they did not want to see a Democratic Congress if Clinton is re-elected.

When asked what party they will support for Congress, voters support Democrats by a margin of 48 percent to 44 percent. The Times poll earlier in the month had Democrats leading by six percentage points.
At the same time, however, 55 percent of voters said they disapproved of the current Republican-controlled Congress, and 48 percent said the Republicans did not deserve continued control of Congress.
